reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This dispatch methodology inherits directly from Unix philosophy (small, composable tools) and modern continuous integration theory. The 'barrel export' pattern mirrors modular arithmetic in abstract algebra, where independent subgroups are merged into a larger ring. The explicit rejection of snapshot trust in favor of git history echoes cryptographic proof-of-work systems, establishing a verifiable chain of custody for code artifacts. The handling of the doubleheader bug reflects historical lessons from database normalization theory, specifically the avoidance of partial dependencies in candidate keys.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The orchestrator (GROK-ORCH) models the development team as a collection of heterogeneous agents with distinct capability manifolds. Workers are viewed as stochastic executors prone to context leakage, hence the strict 'forbidden zone' rules. CLAUDE is modeled as a high-fidelity judgment oracle, reserved exclusively for p-side changes and complex audits. The system anticipates adversarial behavior not from malice, but from entropy—developers naturally drifting into overlapping namespaces. By pre-defining merge orders and isolating judgment lanes, the orchestrator minimizes the cognitive load required for conflict resolution, treating human attention as a scarce, non-renewable resource within the sprint window.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists between the 'free fleet' (PUBLIC cards) and the 'paid path' (INTERNAL logic). The system explicitly forbids any echo of internal context in public-facing diffs, acting as an information-theoretic firewall. Furthermore, the settlement bug triggers a hard stop condition (§5.7) for free-path backfills until the key-space dimensionality is corrected. This cross-layer veto prevents a localized indexing failure in the grading engine from corrupting the global economic incentives of the platform. The requirement for deterministic verify commands (green tests) before squash-merging serves as a final orthogonal check, ensuring that syntactic correctness does not mask semantic violations of the conformance suite.
